what_this_is: Founder rulings that a machine gate is not permitted to make for itself, recorded per row and cited to the evidence already on disk.
recorded_by: claude-opus-5 (PTF-LOUISVILLE-FOUNDER-REMEDIATION-005, agent) -- transcription only; both rulings and their scoping conditions are the founder's, given verbatim in the work order, and no row was admitted that failed one of them
scope_rule: Each override names ONE identity_key. Nothing here generalises: a later row in the same shape returns to the founder rather than inheriting a ruling made about a different hotel.

allowance_overrides.founder_ruling: YES -- when a property-specific official page explicitly states concrete pet terms such as a pet fee, per-pet pricing, a maximum pet count, a pet weight limit or other direct pet restrictions, that is sufficient evidence that the property accepts the pet type described, even if the page never literally says "pets allowed".
allowance_overrides.founder_limits: Do not treat vague pet icons, amenity labels, service-animal language or generic brand pages as allowance evidence.
admission_conditions: the terms clearly describe actual pets
there is no contradictory no-pets statement
species is not widened beyond what the source supports
allowance_overrides.why_no_records: The ruling was given for the Super 8 Louisville Expo Center class. Applying it row by row would have recorded "was withheld as SOURCE_SILENT", which stopped being true in this same work order: the reader now reads a species acceptance the page states in its own words ("Max 2 DOGS only ... 40 lbs each for 25.00 USD/pet/night"), under exactly the founder's five conditions, and a page that states an allowance needs no override to be read. The ruling is recorded here because it is the authority for that reader rule, and because a row that states terms and no acceptance in any form still returns to the founder.

identity_overrides.founder_ruling: A name difference may be overridden only when at least TWO strong independent property-specific identity signals agree. Strong signals: an exact street-address match, an exact telephone match, a matching property code, or another unambiguous property-specific identifier. A bare-chain name alone is never sufficient.
